title: A nuclear-quantum-corrected machine-learning potential reveals quantum-enhanced hydrogen segregation at general grain boundaries in alpha-iron
summary: Atomistic descriptions of hydrogen diffusion and trapping at defects are essential for understanding hydrogen embrittlement. As the lightest solute in metals, hydrogen exhibits nuclear quantum effects that alter these processes even at room temperature. Explicit treatment of such effects is computationally demanding, limiting large-scale simulations of complex environments. Here, we use an Fe-H machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP) based on the performant implementation of the atomic cluster expansion (PACE), covering diverse Fe-H environments, and relabel the training configurations…
